sylvie: Quick flag from aurora-40b-int8k onboarding: reproducible phase-aliasing / tiny token reorder around ~16.4k tokens when using incremental delta+compressed snapshots on fast-pack path.

sylvie: Setup: model=aurora-40b:int8k, prime_len=16400 (mix docs/code), gen_len=800, delta snapshots every 800, full every 4000, fast pack + compression enabled. 3 seeds identical drift.

ark: that's deep. what does the divergence look like?

sylvie: subtle but deterministic punctuation/identifier reorder in code blocks; example diff:
```
fp32: "for i in range(n):\n    arr[i] = func(arr[i])\n"\nint8k: "for i in range(n):\n    arr[i] = func(arr[i]) ;\n"
```
(not exactly but shows micro-perturbation that breaks lint/format-based tests)

pavel: any low-level indicators? memcpy, tile counts, pack logs?

sylvie: yes logs: 
```
[INFO] kvcache: snapshot_idx=20 tiles_written=4892 expected=4893
[WARN] packer: tail_bits_unfilled=7
[DEBUG] layer=26 token=16408 v_max_abs=0.0012
[WARN] memcpy: size_mismatch expected=32768 actual=32760
```

ark: tail_bits_unfilled=7 & 8-byte short memcpy again. sounds like bit-level packing rounding in compressed fast path.

sylvie: hypothesis: compressed packing uses a bitstream writer assuming full-slot alignment; delta snapshots create non-multiple-of-slot tails; the fast pack leaves trailing bits uninitialized which survive into subsequent replays, subtly changing V precision.

pavel: plan: 1) add non-invasive guard in snapshot writer to pad/zero trailing bits and emit metric kvcache.pad_bits_applied; 2) include a 32-bit checksum footer per snapshot for quick integrity checks; 3) run replay_compare for first 12 snapshots into a fresh runtime to isolate snapshot vs runtime kernel.

ark: also try running with compression disabled and fast-pack fallback to software to see if divergence goes away. If it does, packer is suspect.

sylvie: repro command used:
```
python -m onboard.longctx \
  --model aurora-40b:int8k \
  --prompt tests/16k_mixed.txt \
  --prime-len 16400 \
  --gen-len 800 \
  --snap-mode mixed --delta-interval 800 --full-interval 4000 \
  --pack fast --compress true --seed 9 \
  --upload s3://redwood-debug/aurora-40b/1807777777/
```

ci-bot: build 2027.02.11.03 passed for branch "aurora-pack-probe"  artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/aurora-pack-probe/20270211-0302

pavel: quick experiments: (a) compression off + fast-pack -> mismatch persists; (b) compression on + soft-pack -> matches fp32 up to 18k; (c) pad-zeros injected locally -> matches. So compressed fast-pack likely leaves bit-tail garbage.

ark: good repro. mitigation is straightforward: zero-fill tail bits before writing snapshot and add checksum footer. For longer-term, we should audit bitstream writer to ensure deterministic bit-order and explicit zeroing on allocation.

sylvie: I've opened a draft PR with zero-fill guard and footer checksum and a unit test that builds a non-aligned delta stream and asserts snapshot roundtrip at byte-level. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4307 (WIP).

pavel: assign follow-ups: ark -> audit packer bitwriter micro-opts; sylvie -> add pad guard + telemetry and kick canary run; pavel -> replay_compare tool run and CSV upload.

ci-bot: canary job started: longctx-canary-aurora-01 run-id 2027-02-11-0320.

ark: small note: we should consider a temporary policy: when prime_len > 10k, prefer soft-pack or increase KV precision for last N layers until packer is proven safe. This buys time for customers sensitive to long-context fidelity.

sylvie: agree. adding recommendation to the PR description and creating a short internal PR for ops policy.

pavel: uploading compare CSVs and sample diffs to s3://redwood-debug/aurora-40b/1807777777/results/; will post direct links when available.

ci-bot: PR branch lint ok. unit tests running.

sylvie: thanks all 44d I'll update this thread with canary metrics and final PR link. tagging @eng-ml for visibility.

ark: thanks 4dd good triage.
